evidence.claim: In March 2022, an AKP-backed electoral law lowered the parliamentary threshold from 10% to 7%, changed seat allocation among alliances, and exempted the president from rules limiting the use of state resources in campaigns.
evidence.title: Turkey Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: In March 2022, an AKP-backed electoral law lowered the parliamentary threshold from 10% to 7%, changed seat allocation among alliances, and exempted the president from rules limiting the use of state resources in campaigns.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Freedom House gives a dated country-specific summary of an enacted law and its political effect; the claim is concrete and directly tied to the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 legislative changes, published in the next annual report cycle.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Erdogan because the AKP-led majority passed the law and the president benefited from the exemption, though the measure was enacted by parliament rather than by decree.
contrary_evidence: Opposition parties argued the reform was designed to hinder a broad opposition alliance ahead of the 2023 elections.

evidence.claim: The report says Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was convicted in December 2022, Canan Kaftancioglu's conviction was upheld in May, and the Kavala case showed continued disregard for ECHR rulings.
evidence.title: Turkey Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.excerpt: The report says Istanbul mayor Ekrem Imamoglu was convicted in December 2022, Canan Kaftancioglu's conviction was upheld in May, and the Kavala case showed continued disregard for ECHR rulings.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The report names the actors, dates, and legal outcomes and links them to political motivation and judicial control.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 court actions and their political context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Erdogan because the cases targeted his main opposition and civil-society critics within a judicial system the report describes as politically constrained.
contrary_evidence: The government and courts maintained the cases were ordinary criminal proceedings.

evidence.claim: Amnesty said the law tightened government control over social media and news websites and could send people to prison for up to three years for reposting content, creating a chilling effect.
evidence.title: Turkey Dark day for online free expression as new disinformation law is passed
evidence.excerpt: Amnesty said the law tightened government control over social media and news websites and could send people to prison for up to three years for reposting content, creating a chilling effect.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Immediate contemporaneous rights analysis from a major NGO describing the law's likely effect and enforcement risk.
evidence.period_fit: Directly tied to a 2022 statute and its immediate adoption.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the AKP-led government under Erdogan because the law was a state policy choice and part of a broader censorship pattern.
contrary_evidence: The government presented the law as an anti-disinformation measure ahead of elections.

evidence.claim: The Venice Commission said the draft criminal provision interfered with freedom of expression and that there was no pressing social need to introduce it.
evidence.title: Turkiye draft criminal provision on false or misleading information interferes with freedom of expression says Venice Commission
evidence.excerpt: The Venice Commission said the draft criminal provision interfered with freedom of expression and that there was no pressing social need to introduce it.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official Council of Europe opinion summarizing the legal defect in a draft law that was under active consideration in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about a 2022 draft and the legal review that followed.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to the Erdogan government because the draft came from the Turkish state and the warning was about its use against speech.
contrary_evidence: Turkish authorities argued the draft was needed to address misinformation and protect election integrity.

evidence.claim: The report says police used riot shields, tear gas, pepper spray, and detentions against demonstrators, and in Diyarbakir authorities detained 24 women's rights activists, 11 of whom were later arrested.
evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Turkey
evidence.excerpt: The report says police used riot shields, tear gas, pepper spray, and detentions against demonstrators, and in Diyarbakir authorities detained 24 women's rights activists, 11 of whom were later arrested.
evidence.source_locator: report narrative on protests and Diyarbakir arrests
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual U.S. government report with concrete incident reporting and a specific target-year pattern of protest suppression and activist arrests.
evidence.period_fit: Targets 2022 incidents even though the report was published in the next calendar year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable in part to Erdogan because the security and judicial organs operated under his government; the immediate acts were by police and prosecutors.
contrary_evidence: Authorities treated the actions as policing and anti-terror enforcement rather than repression.

evidence.claim: HRW said Kavala and seven co-defendants were sentenced in a sham trial and that the verdict was proof Turkey's courts were operating under instructions from the Erdogan presidency.
evidence.title: Turkey Life Sentence for Rights Defender Osman Kavala
evidence.excerpt: HRW said Kavala and seven co-defendants were sentenced in a sham trial and that the verdict was proof Turkey's courts were operating under instructions from the Erdogan presidency.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct rights-organization statement on a major political case with explicit attribution and contemporaneous legal context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to Erdogan because the case targeted one of his most prominent civil-society critics and the organization says the judiciary was acting under presidential direction.
contrary_evidence: The Turkish court and government said the case was based on serious criminal allegations.

evidence.claim: The EU said the European Court of Human Rights had found Kavala's arrest and pretrial detention pursued an ulterior purpose to silence him and dissuade other human rights defenders.
evidence.title: Turkey Statement by the High Representative on the conviction of Mr. Osman Kavala
evidence.excerpt: The EU said the European Court of Human Rights had found Kavala's arrest and pretrial detention pursued an ulterior purpose to silence him and dissuade other human rights defenders.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official EU statement summarizing a binding ECtHR ruling and the resulting rule-of-law concern.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to the Erdogan government because the EU statement concerns the state's handling of a politically sensitive defendant.
contrary_evidence: Turkey had not implemented the ECHR ruling and maintained the prosecution was lawful.

evidence.claim: Gulsen was jailed pending trial after a joke about religious schools, and critics said the case targeted her liberal views and support for LGBT+ rights.
evidence.title: Turkish pop star's arrest over religious schools quip stirs fierce criticism
evidence.excerpt: Gulsen was jailed pending trial after a joke about religious schools, and critics said the case targeted her liberal views and support for LGBT+ rights.
evidence.source_locator: article body / critics and background paragraphs
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire reporting is contemporaneous and specific, but it remains secondary reporting rather than a legal record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Erdogan-era climate because the arrest was made by Turkish authorities and critics linked it to government-aligned social control, though the immediate decision came from prosecutors and a court.
contrary_evidence: Authorities said the prosecution concerned incitement to hatred rather than her political views.

evidence.claim: Same-sex relations are legal, but Turkish law does not explicitly protect sexual orientation or gender identity, and equality protections do not reliably hold in practice.
evidence.title: Turkiye Treatment of persons with diverse sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, and sex characteristics (SOGIESC) by society and state authorities, including state protection (2020-November 2022)
evidence.publisher: Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada
evidence.excerpt: Same-sex relations are legal, but Turkish law does not explicitly protect sexual orientation or gender identity, and equality protections do not reliably hold in practice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official country-information review compiled from multiple sources; useful for legal status and protection gaps, though it is a secondary synthesis.
evidence.period_fit: Directly covers 2020-November 2022 and thus fits the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Erdogan-era state because the legal and protection environment described is the product of current government policy and enforcement choices.
contrary_evidence: The constitution contains a general equality principle, and same-sex relations are not criminalized.

unresolved_gaps: Direct 2022 Turkish nuclear command-and-control or custody evidence is absent; the dossier mostly shows inherited treaty/NATO/IAEA posture plus civil-nuclear and mediation choices.
Direct forensic or documentary proof of Erdoğan's own assets, beneficial ownership, or personal enrichment in 2022 is still missing.
Independent corroboration beyond Reuters-style reporting is still thin for the media-control and family-access claims.
Audit-grade verification of project delivery and personnel effects is still thin; the package leans heavily on official program documents and self-reported completion counts.
